Subject: 11/12 service disruption — OKR impact and QBR prep

Team —

Following up after the incident on 11/12 where we had the 3.5-hour disruption for hosted inference in us-west-2. Leadership asked for a concise exec brief and a clear set of actions we can present in the QBR on 11/30. High level asks:

- One-paragraph incident recap for execs (what happened, customer impact, duration).
- Top 3 mitigations and owners we can commit to inside the next 90 days.
- Clear note on OKR hit/gap for Reliability (Objective: 99.95% prod availability) and any proposed stretch or corrective key results.

I've attached a draft postmortem (postmortem-draft-v4.pdf) and a starter QBR deck (qbr-slide-deck-11_30.pptx). Please review and push comments to the doc link below.

Priority: Vivek asked for a one-page exec summary by EOD 11/29 so we can circulate to the board. Can each owner confirm the mitigation owner and a realistic ETA?

Thanks —
Vanessa Ortiz
VP, Product Operations
Redwood Inference

Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: 11/12 service disruption — OKR impact and QBR prep

Vanessa —

Thanks for pulling this together. Quick technical summary to drop into the exec one-pager:

- Incident cause: regression in autoscaler (lane-split heuristic) + delayed fallback to reserve pool caused head-of-queue build-up for the orchestrator; KV cache pressure amplified tail latency.
- Customer impact: Host-mode text generation latency >5s for ~18% of requests; several long-tail customer sessions timed out. Estimated customer-facing error budget burn: ~0.03% availability for the month.
- Duration: 2026-11-12 02:14 - 05:42 UTC (root cause fixed at 04:35 UTC; full traffic normalization 05:42 UTC).

Actionable items I recommend for the next 90 days (owner / ETA):
1) Autoscaler fixes + additional unit tests for lane-split heuristic — Owner: Marissa — ETA: 2027-01-15.
2) Circuit-breaker for orchestrator queue depth + alert tuning — Owner: Rishi — ETA: 2026-12-20.
3) KV-cache eviction policy to prefer hot prefixes + canary rollout of 2.1 cache engine — Owner: Platform Eng — ETA: 2027-02-10.

I'll turn the above into bullets for the exec one-pager and post into the draft. Also attaching the raw action log (incident-action-log.csv) for reference.

-Rishi

Attachments: incident-action-log.csv (CSV, 12KB)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 14:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: 11/12 service disruption — OKR impact and QBR prep

Adding implementation context and risks for the QBR slide notes:

- Autoscaler fix details: small patch to lane-split calculation plus an integration test that simulates uneven queueing. Risk: rolling this without canary risks transient regressions; propose canary to 10% capacity, monitor tail latency for 48h.
- CB + alert tuning: low effort, high impact. We'll add an immediate alert for queue depth crossing 95th percentile and a synthetic-configured rate-limiter at the ingress shard.
- KV-cache change: requires a coordinated migration and compatibility tests with existing quantized models; longer runway.

Owners/commitments I can sign up for:
- Implement autoscaler unit and integration tests and ship patch to canary: Marissa — ETA 2026-12-10.
- Prepare canary rollout plan and monitoring dashboards: Marissa & Observability — ETA 2026-12-17.

Vanessa — I updated the draft deck with the mitigation bullets and a slide showing OKR impact. See slide 7.

-Marissa
